net_new_friction.name: Gladly
net_new_friction.primary_blocker: No free self-serve developer sandbox (requires an active customer Admin to create an API User and generate a Basic Auth token, or CSM purchase for a sandbox); additionally, Gladly's official OAuth2 MCP server is gated behind account-team enablement.

net_new_friction.name: Magento (Adobe Commerce)
net_new_friction.primary_blocker: Fragmented auth and API surfaces across PaaS/Open Source (per-store OAuth 1.0a Admin setup and custom store URLs) versus Adobe Commerce as a Cloud Service (Adobe IMS OAuth 2.0 and differing REST endpoints).

net_new_friction.name: Squarespace
net_new_friction.primary_blocker: Third-party OAuth requires client registration and review with 7-day rotating refresh tokens, API keys require paid merchant plans, Webhook Subscriptions are OAuth-only, and official MCP Commerce tools are currently limited to Claude and ChatGPT.

net_new_friction.name: Ecwid
net_new_friction.primary_blocker: Public OAuth2 apps require Ecwid App Market submission, partner agreement, validation review, and a corporate entity for AI apps, while direct custom-app Bearer token access requires users to be on a paid Ecwid plan and manually supply store_id and secret_token.

net_new_friction.name: Binance
net_new_friction.primary_blocker: Requires per-request HMAC/RSA/Ed25519 cryptographic signing, faces HTTP 418 IP-based rate-limit bans on shared cloud egress IPs, and the official MCP server requires browser OAuth plus manual Agentic sub-account funding with no published tools/list schema.

net_new_friction.name: iPayX
net_new_friction.primary_blocker: Contradictory API documentation (two different Supabase Edge Function REST base URLs, two different MCP URLs, mismatched /audit request schemas, and conflicting pricing/rate-limit tiers across /developers, /docs/mcp-server, and /pricing), paid gating on full forensic spread breakdowns, and draft API Terms of Service pending legal review.

net_new_outreach.name: DealCloud
net_new_outreach.primary_blocker: No self-serve developer sandbox or trial; requires an enterprise DealCloud tenant with admin/CSM-provisioned API permissions, plus Celeste licensing and Account Manager approval for local or third-party MCP integrations.

net_new_outreach.name: Salesforce Commerce Cloud
net_new_outreach.primary_blocker: Requires an enterprise B2C Commerce customer instance or paid LINK Technology Partner Program membership (with mandatory Integration Security Review and Certification) to provision credentials and distribute integrations, alongside split Shopper (SLAS) and Admin (Account Manager) auth flows.

net_new_outreach.name: Waterfall.io
net_new_outreach.primary_blocker: No self-serve API key provisioning; Waterfall manually reviews every access request and works with a limited number of approved customers.

net_new_outreach.name: Paygent Connect
net_new_outreach.primary_blocker: Merchant/ISO onboarding and partner-gated NMI gateway provisioning required for API security keys; no official MCP server.

net_new_blocked.name: Sherlock
net_new_blocked.primary_blocker: No hosted public web API; Sherlock is a local CLI and Python HTTP-probing library (with only an unhosted DRF repo and third-party Apify scraper wrappers).

net_new_blocked.name: Mermaid CLI
net_new_blocked.primary_blocker: No public web API or official MCP for mermaid-cli: it is strictly a local CLI and Puppeteer-based Node.js tool (distinct from the separate commercial Mermaid Chart SaaS API and MCP server on mermaid.ai).

sample_pass2_diffs.name: Salesforce
sample_pass2_diffs.reason: The live extracted Salesforce REST API Developer Guide (https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.api_rest.meta/api_rest/intro_oauth_and_connected_apps.htm) explicitly includes 'Generating an OpenAPI 3.0 Document for sObjects REST API (Beta)' in its official documentation navigation.

sample_pass2_diffs.name: Pipedrive
sample_pass2_diffs.reason: The official Pipedrive CRM API page (https://www.pipedrive.com/en/features/crm-api) explicitly states developers can access what they need via webhooks and API endpoints.

sample_pass2_diffs.name: Copper
sample_pass2_diffs.reason: Copper's pricing page (copper.com/pricing) and partner FAQ (copper.com/partners) confirm self-serve account signup with API & Embedded integration SDK gated to paid Professional/Business plans, and partners required to purchase a Business license for a demo account.

sample_pass2_diffs.name: Zendesk
sample_pass2_diffs.reason: Zendesk's official API authentication article (https://support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/4408831452954-How-can-I-authenticate-API-requests) explicitly documents Zendesk webhooks, the Add webhook configuration page, Test webhook functionality, and OAuth authentication for webhooks.

sample_pass2_diffs.name: Pylon
sample_pass2_diffs.reason: Pylon's official pricing page (https://www.usepylon.com/pricing) explicitly lists Webhooks under Developer platform features as included on Professional, Advanced, and Enterprise plans.

sample_pass2_diffs.name: Front
sample_pass2_diffs.reason: https://dev.frontapp.com/docs/partnering-with-front explicitly states developers can sign up for a free development account (so no paid customer account is required to build), while public integrations for Front customers must use OAuth and undergo technical approval (and potential security/legal review) to be published in the Front App Store.

sample_pass2_diffs.name: Plain
sample_pass2_diffs.reason: Plain exposes a GraphQL-only API (https://core-api.uk.plain.com/graphql/v1) with a GraphQL SDL schema at https://core-api.uk.plain.com/graphql/v1/schema.graphql, not a REST OpenAPI specification.

sample_pass2_diffs.name: Help Scout
sample_pass2_diffs.reason: Help Scout's Free plan explicitly excludes API access and integrations (docs.helpscout.com/article/1140-mailbox-api and helpscout.com/pricing/); paid Standard, Plus, or Pro plans are required for API/MCP access, and Plus/Pro is required for Reporting endpoints.

sample_pass2_diffs.name: Twilio
sample_pass2_diffs.reason: The primary doc https://www.twilio.com/docs/usage/requests-to-twilio explicitly covers how the Twilio APIs handle webhooks, and the live Composio production catalog confirms 45 webhook/event triggers.

sample_pass2_diffs.name: Telegram
sample_pass2_diffs.reason: The live Telegram Bot API documentation at https://core.telegram.org/bots/api/ explicitly documents webhooks as one of the two supported methods for receiving bot updates (alongside getUpdates), including webhook URL, port, and max_webhook_connections configuration.

sample_pass2_diffs.name: Aircall
sample_pass2_diffs.reason: Primary Aircall sources (https://aircall.io/pricing/ FAQ and https://aircall.io/blog/tech/ai-ecosystem-developer-guide/) explicitly confirm Aircall offers an open webhook framework for real-time call and contact events set up after user authorization.

sample_pass2_diffs.name: Vonage
sample_pass2_diffs.reason: The live Getting Started Overview doc (https://developer.vonage.com/en/getting-started/overview) explicitly states under the OpenAPI section: 'Each of our APIs has its own OpenAPI specification.'

sample_pass2_diffs.name: SendGrid
sample_pass2_diffs.reason: The official SendGrid v3 API reference (https://www.twilio.com/docs/sendgrid/api-reference) explicitly lists an OpenAPI specification under SDKs and tools.

sample_pass2_diffs.name: MrScraper

sample_pass2_diffs.name: GitHub

sample_pass2_diffs.name: Clay

sample_pass2_diffs.name: Notion
sample_pass2_diffs.reason: Notion's official pricing page (https://www.notion.com/pricing) explicitly lists Webhooks under API automations & integrations alongside Public API, corroborated by 8 triggers in the Composio production catalog.

sample_pass2_diffs.name: Linear

sample_pass2_diffs.name: Monday.com
sample_pass2_diffs.reason: The primary developer documentation (https://developer.monday.com/api-reference/docs/getting-started and https://developer.monday.com/api-reference/docs/build-on-monday-with-ai) specifies that Monday.com exposes a single-endpoint GraphQL API (https://api.monday.com/v2) using a GraphQL schema and schema introspection rather than REST or an OpenAPI specification.

sample_pass2_diffs.name: ClickUp
sample_pass2_diffs.reason: ClickUp's official FAQ (https://clickup.com/faqs) explicitly states that webhook support is available alongside its public REST API and OAuth, corroborated by 21 triggers in the live Composio production catalog.

sample_pass2_diffs.name: Xero
sample_pass2_diffs.reason: The live Xero Developer Pricing page (https://developer.xero.com/pricing) explicitly lists Webhooks under Standard features across all plans (Starter, Core, Plus, Advanced, and Enterprise).
